book_name: Idle Thoughts of an Idle Fellow

PREFACE

One or two friends to whom I showed these papers in MS. having observed
that they were not half bad, and some of my relations having promised to
buy the book if it ever came out, I feel I have no right to longer delay
its issue. But for this, as one may say, public demand, I perhaps should
not have ventured to offer these mere "idle thoughts" of mine as mental
food for the English-speaking peoples of the earth. What readers ask
nowadays in a book is that it should improve, instruct, and elevate.
This book wouldn't elevate a cow. I cannot conscientiously recommend it
for any useful purposes whatever. All I can suggest is that when you get
tired of reading "the best hundred books," you may take this up for half
an hour. It will be a change.




CONTENTS.

     IDLE THOUGHTS OF AN IDLE FELLOW.

     ON BEING IDLE
     ON BEING IN LOVE
     ON BEING IN THE BLUES
     ON BEING HARD UP
     ON VANITY AND VANITIES
     ON GETTING ON IN THE WORLD
     ON THE WEATHER
     ON CATS AND DOGS
     ON BEING SHY
     ON BABIES
     ON EATING AND DRINKING
     ON FURNISHED APARTMENTS
     ON DRESS AND DEPORTMENT
     ON MEMORY




THE IDLE THOUGHTS OF AN IDLE FELLOW.
generated_text:
A few kind souls who suffered through these scribblings in manuscript form remarked—with what I can only assume was pity—that they weren’t entirely dreadful. Meanwhile, certain relatives, possibly out of obligation or a misplaced sense of loyalty, swore they’d purchase a copy if it ever stumbled into print. With such overwhelming public pressure (if one can call two friends and a guilt-tripped aunt “the public”), who am I to withhold these utterly pointless musings from the English-speaking world?

Modern readers demand books that edify, enlighten, and uplift. This one would struggle to uplift a feather, let alone a cow. I cannot, in good conscience, recommend it for intellectual, moral, or even kindling-related purposes. However, if you ever weary of trudging through the so-called “Great Books” (and let’s be honest, who doesn’t?), you might flip through this for a bit. It’ll make a nice change—like swapping a three-hour lecture for a nap.
